published_statement: RIEMANNIAN / TIME-SYMMETRIC (Schoen-Yau 1979, restated 1704.05490 Thm 1.1, 5.3): Let (M^n, g) be a complete asymptotically flat Riemannian manifold, g_ij = delta_ij + O(|x|^-p), |x||dg| + |x|^2|d^2 g| = O(|x|^-p), p > (n-2)/2, |R| = O(|x|^-q), q > n, with scalar curvature R >= 0. Then the ADM mass m = (1/(4(n-1) omega_{n-1})) lim int_{S_sigma} (g_ij,i - g_ii,j) nu^j is >= 0 for each end, and if any mass is zero then (M,g) is isometric to R^n. SPACETIME (Schoen-Yau 1981 E >= 0 n=3; Witten 1981 E >= |P| n=3 spin; EHLS 2016 Thm 1 E >= |P| for 3 <= n < 8 no spin): Let (M,g,k) be a complete asymptotically flat initial data set (g - delta in W^{2,p}_{-q}, k in W^{1,p}_{-1-q}, q in ((n-2)/2, n-2), mu, J in C^{0,alpha}_{-n-q0}) satisfying the dominant energy condition mu >= |J|_g, where 2 mu = R - |k|^2 + (tr k)^2 and J = div k - d(tr k). Then E >= |P|. Rigidity (E = |P| => E = P = 0 and (M,g,k) embeds in Minkowski): proven for spin manifolds (Beig-Chruściel 1996 n=3; Chruściel-Maerten 2006 all n), and R^3 is spin, so in the n = 3 case the tree uses it is a theorem; EHLS 2016 p.2 records it as conjectural for non-spin n > 3 at that date. In the STATIC case the tree seats (k = 0): P = 0, E = M_ADM, J = 0, and the DEC reduces to mu >= 0, i.e. R >= 0 -- the weak energy condition and the DEC coincide there.
published_hypotheses: H1 completeness: (M,g) complete, no boundary (or boundary handled separately); finitely many ends allowed.

H2 asymptotic flatness with stated decay: g - delta = O(|x|^-p), p > (n-2)/2 (n=3: p > 1/2), derivatives one order faster each; scalar curvature / mu, J integrable (|R| = O(|x|^-q), q > n). Without this the ADM integral is undefined or coordinate-dependent.
H3 energy condition: DEC mu >= |J| for initial data; R >= 0 in the time-symmetric case. This is the only hypothesis about matter, and it is pointwise.
H4 dimension / topology: originally n = 3 (Schoen-Yau 1979/1981) or spin (Witten 1981); 3 <= n < 8 (Schoen 1989, EHLS 2016); all n without spin (Schoen-Yau 2017, Lohkamp 2016).
H5 regularity: g in C^2_loc, k in C^1_loc (EHLS Def. 3); later relaxed (continuous metrics 2606.19123, distributional 2606.23272 -- not read).
Conclusion is about the TOTAL quantity E (or m) at spatial infinity only; the theorem says nothing about the sign of any local density or of the enclosed mass at finite radius.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis -- that the authors lacked data -- tested for THIS result: the positive mass theorem takes no datum. Its inputs are a manifold, a metric, a symmetric tensor and the inequality mu >= |J|; nothing measured between 1979 and 2026 enters it, so no later measurement can move its conclusion. Evidence: the statement in 1110.2087 Thm 1 and 1704.05490 Thm 1.1 contains no physical constant, and the only external 'fact' it rests on -- that matter satisfies the DEC -- is not assumed silently but NAMED as hypothesis H3. What the authors 'lacked' in the sense M means is therefore not data but scope: (a) the dimension/spin restriction, since lifted (Schoen-Yau 2017, Lohkamp 2016) -- the theorem got LARGER, not smaller; (b) the sharpness of H3, settled by Jaracz 2022: WEC is not enough, so the hypothesis is load-bearing, not a convenience; (c) whether quantum matter violates the DEC -- known in 1979 (Epstein-Glaser-Jaffe 1965, Casimir) and not a lacuna of the proof: a theorem with a named hypothesis is not refuted by matter that fails the hypothesis, it is silent about it. Conclusion: having any later datum does not change the theorem; it changes only whether the theorem APPLIES, and on the warp board it does not apply to any seated configuration -- the tree's own certify.py reports every one outside H3. That silence cuts both ways and the tree currently uses it in one direction only (the M_ADM = 0 corridor 'not forbidden', the bare negative mass 'forbidden'). M's hypothesis is not confirmed for this result: the mathematics is not incomplete or wrong; the board's reading of which hypothesis carries the weight is.
grade_evidence: The theorem as PUBLISHED stands and has only widened since 1979-81 (all dimensions, no spin; rigidity proven for the n = 3 spin case the tree uses); no counterexample within its hypotheses exists and the rederivation reproduces every owner datum but one recorded discrepancy. The tree's USE holds on a smaller class than the tree states: (1) the DEC hypothesis H3 is dropped at certify.py:161-164/:487-489, overturn.py:196/:207/:649-650, phase1.py:195-197/:397-399/:537-539, concentric.py:7-8/:49-50 -- named only in pair.py:103-108/:306-308 and conceded in concentric.py:51-53/:126-133; (2) phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8 infer from the theorem a prohibition on a bare negative mass that the theorem does not give once H3 fails -- z3 (script section D, case i) shows the inference is not derivable, Jaracz 2022 Thm 1.2 and Hao et al. 2023 show negative ADM mass is realised when H3 is dropped, and the tree's own certify.py shows the corridor phase1 admits fails H3 exactly as the candidate it excludes does; (3) 'not violated / never in danger / has nothing to object to' (certify.py:163-164, concentric.py:271-273, :352-354) are true statements whose truth is vacuous -- the theorem does not apply to a DEC-violating configuration in either direction. Not WRONG: nothing is refuted and the one numerical mismatch (concentric.py:50-51 header) is a discrepancy, not a refutation. Not STANDS: a hypothesis the tree drops is load-bearing (Jaracz 2022). Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum. Not OPEN: the statement was read at source via exact restatements and the finite parts were machine-checked.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: each of the four owners states H3 (and H1/H2) at the point of use, and phase1.py:397-399 / concentric.py:7-8 are reworded from 'forbidden by the positive mass theorem' to 'excluded IF the DEC is imposed -- which no candidate on this board satisfies', with phase1.ranked() then excluding or admitting the bare-negative-mass and M_ADM = 0 candidates on the same criterion (a text repair; under the chat-67 hold it needs M's ruling, and this audit does not make it). To WRONG: a complete AF initial data set with the DEC and E < 0, or with E = 0 not Minkowski in n = 3 -- this would overturn four independent proofs (Schoen-Yau minimal surfaces, Witten spinors, Jang equation, MOTS) and nothing in the literature read here suggests one. To DATA-DEPENDENT: not reachable; the theorem has no datum. To OPEN: only if the restatements read here were shown to misquote the originals -- the three restatements agree with one another on every hypothesis.
